name: Two governors for one word (tanāzuʿ)
definition: Two verbs (or words that govern like verbs) before one noun, each needing it: which of them governs it?
body: In 'he struck me, and I struck Zayd', both verbs reach for zayd. The Basrans gave the noun to the second governor, the nearer, and let the first take a pronoun; the Kufans gave it to the first, the earlier. Either may govern; the Alfiyya reports that the Basrans prefer the second and others the first, and the question is one of the classic disputes recorded in al-Inṣāf.

examples.text: He struck me, and I struck Zayd: zaydan is governed by the second verb, the Basran way.
